question: What is the minimum age at which you can get a Class C driver license without either driver education or being a hardship case? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: 25 under the current handbook: everyone younger than 25 must complete an approved driver education course (p.13; Class C table p.10 says applicants 18 to 24 need an approved course). With driver education: provisional license at 16.

question: How much is the maximum fine for a first conviction of driving without a license? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: A fine of up to $200 (Table 7).

question: What type of restrictions may be placed on your license? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: Restrictions meant to make you a safer driver (full list in an appendix), e.g. wearing corrective lenses when the vision exam shows they improve your vision; provisional licenses carry GDL passenger and midnight-5 a.m. limits.

question: In what direction should you turn your wheels when parking uphill without a curb? (Chpt. 7)
handbookAnswer: To the right (toward the edge of the road).

question: What action should you take if you fail to receive the renewal notice card reminding you that your driver license is about to expire? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: Renew anyway: the notice is a courtesy and renewing remains your responsibility.

question: On a one-way street, what color is the broken lane marker? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: White.

question: Describe the "Yield" sign. (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: An equilateral triangle (point down), used only for yield signs, red and white.

question: What does a "Narrow Bridge" sign look like, and how should the driver react when he sees one? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: A yellow diamond warning sign; the bridge ahead is not as wide as the road, so slow down and use caution.

question: What is the shape of a "Keep Right" sign, and how should the driver react when he sees one? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: A vertical rectangle (regulatory sign); drive to the right of the island or median ahead.

question: Which sign tells you to slow down because you are approaching a double curve? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The reverse-curve warning sign (road curves one way, then the other): slow down, keep right, do not pass.

question: What does a "Do Not Pass" sign mean? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: Do not pass other vehicles.

question: Which sign tells you to keep in the right-hand lane when driving slow? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The SLOWER TRAFFIC KEEP RIGHT sign.

question: What does "Yield Right-of-Way" mean? (Chpt. 4, 5)
handbookAnswer: Slow down or stop as needed and let others with the right-of-way go first; right-of-way is given, not taken.

question: Describe the equipment required on passenger cars by state law. (Chpt. 2)
handbookAnswer: Foot brake able to stop within 25 ft at 20 mph plus a parking brake; headlights with beam indicator, two taillights, two (or three) brake lights, license plate light, parking lights, red reflectors, turn signals; horn audible for 200 ft; muffler and (1968+) exhaust emission system; safety glass; front and rear plates; wipers; rearview mirror showing 200 ft behind; front safety belts; tires with at least 2/32 inch tread; fuel cap; SMV emblem on vehicles of 25 mph or less.

question: What is the purpose of an exhaust emission system? (Chpt. 2)
handbookAnswer: To help reduce air pollution (required on 1968 and later models).

question: Describe the types of equipment that Texas state law specifically forbids on passenger cars driven within the state. (Chpt. 2)
handbookAnswer: A red light showing to the front; a bell, siren or exhaust whistle (except emergency vehicles); a muffler cutout; anything extending more than 3 in. beyond the left side or 6 in. beyond the right side; flashing red front lights (except emergency vehicles, school and church buses); a radar or laser interference device.

question: How should you react when a traffic officer tells you to do something that is ordinarily considered to be against the law? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: Obey the officer.

question: Once the brakes have been applied, about how many feet does a car which was going 70 mph travel before it comes to a stop? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: About 233 feet of braking distance (after 154 ft of reaction distance; 387 ft total), per the stopping-distance chart.

question: When is it necessary to stop before proceeding when you overtake a school bus loading or unloading children? (Chpt. 4)
handbookAnswer: Whenever the bus shows alternately flashing red lights (from either direction); stay stopped until it moves, the driver signals you on, or the lights stop. Not required on a different road or at a controlled-access highway loading zone.

question: About how many feet will the average driver going 50 mph travel from the moment he sees danger until he hits the brakes? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: About 110 feet (the average person needs 1½ seconds to think, react and apply the brakes).

question: Within how many feet of a crosswalk may you park, when parking near a corner? (Chpt. 7)
handbookAnswer: No closer than 20 feet.

question: What is the state speed limit for automobiles in urban districts? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: 30 mph.

question: Does a posted speed limit of 55 mph mean that you may drive 55 mph on that highway under all conditions? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: No; limits are for normal conditions, and you must slow down for heavy traffic, bad weather or low visibility (basic speed law).

question: You should never drive on the left half of the roadway when you are within how many feet from an intersection, bridge, or railroad crossing? (Chpt. 6)
handbookAnswer: 100 feet.

question: What should you do if you discover you are in the wrong lane to make a turn as you enter an intersection? (Chpt. 6)
handbookAnswer: Do not turn; continue straight ahead (if you cannot get into the proper lane in time, go on and turn later).

question: When two cars meet at the intersection of a two-lane road with a four-lane road, which one must yield the right-of-way? (Chpt. 4)
handbookAnswer: The car on the two-lane road.

question: If you are driving and hear a siren coming, what should you do? (Chpt. 4)
handbookAnswer: Yield: pull to the right edge of the road and stop; if you can't, slow down and leave a clear path.

question: What is the first thing that should be done when a car starts to skid? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Don't hit the brakes hard; take your foot off the gas, then steer in the direction of the skid.

question: At what time of the day should your headlights be turned on? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and any time people or vehicles can't be seen clearly for 1,000 feet.

question: Under what conditions may your driver license be suspended? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: Mandatory suspension for convictions such as DWI, drug offenses, failure to stop and render aid, racing; DPS may suspend after a hearing for 4+ convictions in 12 months or 7+ in 24, a serious crash, driving while license invalid; ALR for a failed or refused breath or blood test; under-21 alcohol offenses; minors with 2+ convictions in 12 months.

question: What is carbon monoxide, and how may it be harmful to drivers? (Chpt. 14)
handbookAnswer: A deadly gas in vehicle exhaust (colorless, odorless); never run the motor in a garage or sit in a parked running car with windows closed, fix a defective exhaust, and move a victim to fresh air and call 911.

question: Describe what you should do if you have a blowout while driving. (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Don't brake hard; take your foot off the gas, brake gently and steer straight ahead to a stop.

question: What should you do when driving down a steep grade in a car with standard transmission? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Shift into a low gear to help slow the car; never coast in neutral or with your foot on the clutch.

question: What should you do if you damage an unattended vehicle? (Chpt. 11)
handbookAnswer: Stop and find the owner to give your name and address, or securely attach a written note with your name, address and what happened.

question: When are crash reports required? (Chpt. 11)
handbookAnswer: Notify law enforcement as soon as possible if anyone is hurt or killed, the vehicles can't be moved, a driver leaves, or a driver seems intoxicated. The handbook also says a crash not investigated by an officer must be reported in writing to TxDOT within 10 days (pp.65-66; its sentence states the injury/$1,000 condition inverted). That driver-report rule is outdated: former Transportation Code 550.061 was repealed effective Sept. 1, 2017 (SB 312), and TxDOT no longer keeps driver CR-2 reports.

question: If you are required to show proof of financial responsibility for the future, how many years must such proof be kept up? (Chpt. 3)
handbookAnswer: Two years from the most recent conviction date.

question: What type of sign warns you to watch right and left for cross traffic? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: A yellow diamond warning sign: the crossroad sign (slow down and watch for cross traffic in all directions).

question: Describe the emblem that identifies vehicles which travel at speeds of 25 mph or less. (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem: an orange triangle with a red reflective border, for vehicles designed for 25 mph or less.

question: In which gear should you drive when going down a steep hill? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: A low gear.

question: What qualifications must one have to teach a beginner to drive? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: A licensed driver at least 21 with at least one year of driving experience, in the seat beside the driver, not intoxicated or asleep.

question: If the person is under 18, when does his provisional license expire? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: On the 18th birthday.

question: When parked parallel, your curb side wheels must be no more than how many inches from the curb? (Chpt. 7)
handbookAnswer: 18 inches.

question: When following another car, what is a good distance at which you should follow behind? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: At least 2 seconds at 30 mph or less and 4 seconds above 30 mph in good conditions; more in poor conditions.

question: To what agency and within what time period must a change of address be reported for driver licensing purposes? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: To DPS within 30 days.

question: What effects does the use of marijuana and amphetamine have on driving? (Chpt. 10)
handbookAnswer: Marijuana impairs concentration, judgment and sensory/perceptual skills; heavy amphetamine use keeps drivers awake but makes them less coordinated, edgy and more likely to crash.

question: What is the penalty for being convicted of driving while intoxicated? (Chpt. 10)
handbookAnswer: First offense: fine up to $2,000, 72 hours to 180 days in jail and a 90- to 365-day license suspension; more for repeat offenses.

question: What does a green arrow showing with a red light mean? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: You may go carefully in the arrow's direction after yielding to other vehicles and pedestrians.

question: How should you react to a flashing red light? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

question: Which sign tells you to watch out for a train? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The round yellow railroad advance warning sign (and the crossbuck at the crossing).

question: Describe the sign that warns you to slow down for a winding road. (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The winding road warning sign (yellow diamond with a winding arrow): drive slowly and carefully, do not pass.

question: What sign indicates that the road that you are on merges with another? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The merge warning sign (other lanes come together with yours; watch for traffic).

question: What kind of sign warns you that the highest safe speed for the turn ahead is 25 mph? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: An advisory speed sign (yellow, with the curve or turn warning).

question: Describe the sign that tells you to watch for cross traffic ahead. (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The yellow diamond crossroad sign: slow down and watch for cross traffic.

question: What type of sign warns you that you should slow down for a sharp rise in the roadway? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The bump warning sign (sudden high place in the road).

question: Describe the type of sign that would let you know that you were on a short state highway in a city or urban area. (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: A LOOP route marker (white with LOOP above the number): a short state highway in a city or urban area.

question: What is the maximum number of inches you may lawfully allow an object to extend beyond the left fender of your car? (Chpt. 2)
handbookAnswer: 3 inches (6 inches on the right side).

question: Under what conditions must you always stop? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: At stop signs, steady and flashing red lights, a school bus with flashing red lights, railroad signals, gates or flaggers, and when an officer directs you to.

question: What should you do when coming onto a street from a private alley or driveway? (Chpt. 4)
handbookAnswer: Stop before the sidewalk and yield to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

question: If a child runs into the road 45 to 50 feet ahead of your car, what is the highest speed from which you can stop with good brakes without hitting him? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: Not stated directly. The current chart shows 63 ft needed to stop from 20 mph (44 ft reaction + 19 ft braking), so you would have to be going slower than 20 mph.

question: How close to a fireplug may a vehicle lawfully park? (Chpt. 7)
handbookAnswer: No closer than 15 feet.

question: What does a posted speed limit of 55 mph mean? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: The maximum legal speed in good conditions; drive slower when conditions require.

question: What is the maximum speed limit for passenger cars on a Texas Highway numbered by this state or United States outside an urban district? (Chpt. 8)
handbookAnswer: 70 mph (unless posted otherwise).

question: Under what circumstances should you never attempt to pass a car ahead of you? (Chpt. 6)
handbookAnswer: In a no-passing zone or across solid lines; within 100 ft of an intersection, railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct or tunnel; on hills or curves with limited vision; when you can't get back before an oncoming car comes within 200 ft.

question: Under what conditions are overtaking and passing to the right not permitted? (Chpt. 6)
handbookAnswer: Passing on the right only when safe and the road has 2+ clear lanes each way, on a one-way road, or on a paved shoulder around a vehicle that is slowing, stopped, disabled or turning left; never by driving off the pavement.

question: When a driver is waiting to make a left turn, what is the procedure he should take when the light turns green? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: Yield to all traffic coming from the opposite direction, then turn when safe.

question: What precautions should a driver take at uncontrolled intersections? (Chpt. 4)
handbookAnswer: Yield to vehicles that have entered or are approaching from the right, check that nothing is coming from the left, and make sure the other driver yields before you go.

question: What regulations should a bicycle rider observe? (Chpt. 13)
handbookAnswer: Same rights and duties as drivers: obey traffic laws, signs and signals, ride with traffic, keep right when slower (with exceptions), signal turns and stops, ride two abreast only within one lane without impeding traffic, use a front light and rear reflector at night.

question: Under what conditions should headlights be used? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: As in #29; use low beams within 500 ft of an oncoming vehicle, within 300 ft behind another vehicle, on lighted roads, and in fog, rain, sleet, snow or dust.

question: You should dim your lights when you are within how many feet of an approaching car? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: 500 feet.

question: What type of lighting should cars use when parked on the highway at night? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Parking lights or low-beam headlights.

question: Which lights should you use when you are driving in a fog? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Low beams.

question: When are you required to show proof of financial responsibility? (Chpt. 3)
handbookAnswer: When applying for a license, registering a vehicle or getting an inspection, and to a law enforcement officer on request or to another person involved in a crash.

question: When needed, how may one show proof of financial responsibility? (Chpt. 3)
handbookAnswer: A liability policy, a standard proof-of-insurance card, an insurance binder, a $55,000 deposit certificate, a DPS surety bond, a self-insurance certificate, or an image on a wireless device.

question: What sign warns you that you must slow down? (Chpt. 5)
handbookAnswer: Warning signs (yellow diamonds): pay attention and reduce speed to at least the posted advisory speed.

question: What circumstances may lead to possible loss of your license? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: As in #30 (mandatory, administrative and court-ordered suspensions, revocations and cancellations).

question: In addition to mufflers, what new equipment is required on all cars manufactured in 1968 and after? (Chpt. 2)
handbookAnswer: An exhaust emission system (to help reduce air pollution).

question: Why are seat belts important? (Chpt. 14)
handbookAnswer: They keep you from being thrown from the car (five times more likely to be killed if thrown), from hitting the dashboard, and in better control; required for everyone.

question: What is meant by "defensive driving?" (Chpt. 14)
handbookAnswer: Staying alert with eyes moving, looking for trouble spots, having a plan of action, and protecting each other from mistakes.

question: What are the different classes of licenses and age requirements for each? (Chpt. 1)
handbookAnswer: Class A (combinations of 26,001+ lb GCWR towing over 10,000 lb) and Class B (single vehicle 26,001+ lb): 18, or 17 with driver education. Class C (other vehicles: single vehicle under 26,001 lb towing up to 10,000 lb, autocycles): 18 (18-24 need driver ed), 16 with driver ed, 15 with a hardship license. Class M (motorcycles): 16, or 15 for 250 cc or less.

question: When is a bicyclist not required to ride to the right of the roadway? (Chpt. 13)
handbookAnswer: When passing, preparing for a left turn, avoiding unsafe conditions, or in an outside lane under 14 ft wide without a bike lane (or too narrow to share).

question: When are bicyclists allowed to ride two abreast in a traffic lane? (Chpt. 13)
handbookAnswer: On a laned road they must stay within a single lane and not impede traffic (Transportation Code 551.103(c)).

question: What are the three most common motorist caused car-bicycle crashes? (Chpt. 9)
handbookAnswer: Turning left in front of oncoming bicycle traffic; turning right across the bicycle's path; pulling away from a stop sign without yielding to bicycle cross traffic.

question: What are the penalties for minors (persons under the age of 21) convicted of Driving Under the Influence of Alcohol? (Chpt. 10)
handbookAnswer: First offense: Class C misdemeanor, fine up to $500, 20 to 40 hours of community service and an alcohol awareness course; more for repeat offenses.

question: What are the penalties for minors (persons under the age of 21) convicted of non-driving alcohol-related offenses? (Chpt. 10)
handbookAnswer: First offense: Class C misdemeanor, fine up to $500, 8 to 12 hours of community service, alcohol awareness course, 30-day license suspension (60 days for a 2nd, 180 days for a 3rd at 17+).
